newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 24.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on January 24:

WASHINGTON - An expert panel decided not to recommend routine mammograms for women in their forties, concluding that the latest scientific evidence on whether the X-ray test prevents breast cancer is not strong enough to justify such advice.

NEW YORK - Charles Feeney, a reclusive businessman who wanted to remain anonymous, revealed that he has financed a secret philanthropic organisation for more than a decade that has amassed assets of more than $3.5 billion, making it the fourth largest charity in the United States.

WASHINGTON - New United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan met U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee chairman Jesse Helms, and agreed to give Congress unprecedented cooperation in hope of prying loose more than $1 billion owed by the United States to the world body.

BERLIN - The Swiss government endorsed a proposal by one of the country's leading bankers to set up a Holocaust memorial fund of more than $70 million as quickly as possible to compensate survivors of Nazi death camps and heirs of those who died there.

WASHINGTON - Maryland legislative leaders are developing a plan to allow slot machines at racetracks, a move that will test Governor Parris Glendening's resolve to prevent the spread of legalised gambling in the state.
WASHINGTON - While the National Football League won't crown its annual champion until after Sunday's Super Bowl, the season's biggest loser has already been determined: the NFL itself.
